sections.markdown:
## C2 — Signs, work zones and school zones

FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A01
At a School Crossing Ahead warning, slow down and keep watching for children. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A01
The School Crossing sign identifies where children cross and requires stopping when pedestrians are waiting to cross. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A01
At a Pedestrian Crossing warning, reduce speed, watch for people in your path and be ready to stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A01
At a Low Clearance warning, do not proceed if the vehicle is too tall to pass beneath the overpass. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A01
A Hill warning signals a steep grade where the driver should check the brakes and may need a lower gear. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A01
A Divided Highway Begins sign warns of a median separating two one-way roadways and directs drivers to keep right. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A01
A Divided Highway Ends warning means the road becomes a single roadway carrying traffic both ways, where drivers should keep right. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R08 | anchor: A01
At a Deer Crossing warning, stay alert and reduce speed if a deer appears. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R09 | anchor: A01
A Cattle Crossing warning marks a place where livestock is driven between farm areas. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R10 | anchor: A01
At a Slippery When Wet warning, reduce speed, avoid hard braking or abrupt turns and leave more following space. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R11 | anchor: A02
Orange is the basic color used for construction and maintenance traffic-control devices. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-R12 | anchor: A02
Work-area warning signs are mostly diamond-shaped, although some are rectangular. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-R13 | anchor: A02
Construction and maintenance signs warn of unusual or potentially dangerous conditions near work areas and call for a cautious approach. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-R14 | anchor: A02
Exceeding the posted speed in a construction or work zone is a violation. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-R15 | anchor: A02
The diagonal stripes on barricades or vertical panels show the side on which traffic should pass. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-R16 | anchor: A02
Stripes descending toward the right direct traffic to bear right. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-R17 | anchor: A02
Stripes descending toward the left direct traffic to bear left. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-R18 | anchor: A02
Barricades, panels, drums, cones and tubes warn of work-area hazards and guide traffic, often using steady or flashing lights at night. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-R19 | anchor: A03
Work-zone arrow panels can operate by day or night to guide vehicles into lanes and warn that part of the road ahead is closed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-R20 | anchor: A03
Work-zone flaggers may stop, slow or guide traffic through the area. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-R21 | anchor: A03
The handbook describes flaggers wearing orange clothing and directing traffic with red flags or stop-and-slow paddles. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-R22 | anchor: A03
Traffic fines are doubled in work zones. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-R23 | anchor: A03
Construction and work zones have no single standard speed limit; the transportation department, local authority, utility company or private contractor sets a limit for each zone. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-R24 | anchor: A03
Knowingly or negligently driving through a highway construction zone in a way that endangers people or property can lead to a Reckless Endangerment of a Highway Worker charge. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-R25 | anchor: A03
Removing, ignoring or intentionally striking a traffic-control device in the stated highway construction-zone circumstances may also lead to a Reckless Endangerment of a Highway Worker charge. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-R26 | anchor: A04
Check speed and slow near schools at any hour, watching for children near schools and parks during both day and night. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R27 | anchor: A04
School-zone limits may be as low as 15 miles per hour. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R28 | anchor: A04
Drivers must stop and remain stopped for pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R29 | anchor: A04
A school zone includes the campus, adjoining streets and additional surrounding blocks designated by the local authority setting a special limit. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R30 | anchor: A04
Always yield to pedestrians in a school crosswalk, whether or not a crossing guard is present. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R31 | anchor: A04
Stop before a school crosswalk so other drivers can see the pedestrians. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R32 | anchor: A04
Do not drive through a column of schoolchildren crossing a roadway. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R33 | anchor: A04
Do not pass a school crossing guard who is directing children across the road while holding the official sign in its stop position. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R34 | anchor: A04
School-zone signs, road markings and flashing lights can indicate an authorized change in speed limit. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R35 | anchor: A04
School-zone parking and stopping signs can keep travel lanes, sightlines and bus loading zones clear. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R36 | anchor: A04
Speeding fines are doubled in Montana school zones. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R37 | anchor: A04
Children approaching school may cross without understanding traffic controls or accurately judging a vehicle’s speed and distance. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R38 | anchor: A04
School pickup and drop-off congestion can add confusion to parking lots and nearby streets. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]
